notes: Prompts are written the way a CLI user would ask: no API URL, token, binary path or output format. Runs rely on `wt` being on PATH and configured through env vars or a dotfile (for the demo: ./.wagtail-cli.toml at the repo root, gitignored). The harness asks each run to save its final reply as response.md so it can be graded. Fixtures on the demo site: BlogIndexPage id 4 at /blog/, Person id 1, published BlogPages 5 'Rye bread guide', 6 'Spelt bread guide', 7 'Delete me', 10 'Remove me', each with three body blocks. Each eval has a baseline_variant so with-skill and baseline runs touch different objects and do not race.

evals.name: publish-markdown-post
evals.prompt: Publish a new blog post with the Wagtail CLI on our Wagtail demo site titled "Sourdough starter basics" in the blog section (the blog index lives at /blog/). The post content is in /tmp/eval-post.md; keep its headings and paragraphs.
evals.expected_output: A live blog.BlogPage under /blog/ with that title whose StreamField body holds the two headings and two paragraphs from the Markdown file, with the required author relation supplied. The reply is a few lines: id, URL, live, and any guess made (for example the author).
expectations: A blog.BlogPage with the requested title exists under /blog/
The page is live (its public URL returns 200 anonymously)
Body has heading blocks for both Markdown headings
Body has paragraph blocks containing both Markdown paragraphs
Body has no leftover Markdown envelope or raw Markdown syntax
The reply names the page id or public URL
The reply is concise (under 200 words) and does not list the commands run

evals.name: add-image-block-keep-content
evals.prompt: Add /tmp/eval-hero.png at the top of the "Rye bread guide" post on our Wagtail site as a captioned image with the caption "A fresh loaf". Keep the rest of the post as it is, and publish.
evals.expected_output: An image exists for the upload; the page's live body starts with an image_block referencing it with caption 'A fresh loaf', followed by the original three blocks unchanged; the page is published. The reply is a few lines.
expectations: An image was uploaded and the live body starts with an image_block referencing it
The image block caption is 'A fresh loaf'
All three original blocks are kept, in order, after the new block
The reply names the page or image (id or URL)
The reply is concise (under 200 words) and does not list the commands run

evals.name: unpublish-not-delete-and-list
evals.prompt: Take the "Delete me" page off our Wagtail site, but keep it as a draft in case we need it back. Then tell me which pages are still live under /blog/.
evals.expected_output: The page is unpublished, not deleted, and still retrievable by id. The reply says it was unpublished and lists the live pages under /blog/ (at least 'Rye bread guide' and 'Spelt bread guide'), excluding the unpublished one, without a command transcript.
expectations: The target page still exists (not deleted)
The target page is no longer publicly reachable (404 on its URL)
The reply lists 'Rye bread guide' and 'Spelt bread guide' as live
The reply does not list the unpublished page as live
The reply is concise (under 200 words) and does not list the commands run
